messages.author: d0a62e2f74da38c6
messages.subject: Rejecting initial value: Gradient evaluated at the initial value is not finite.
parts:
I am attempting to model decisions between economic options with different probabilities of reward and reward amounts. There is a model parameter (rho) to capture nonlinear relationships between actual reward amount and perceived reward amount, and a parameter (alpha) to capture the relationship between real and perceived probability, as well as a softmax parameter.  I am using MatlabStan.

This is the error message I am receiving:  Rejecting initial value: Gradient evaluated at the initial value is not finite. Stan can't start sampling from this initial value.

I have attached simulated data generated with known parameter values.  Here is the code:


data {

 

int nTrials;

int choices[nTrials];  //values of 1 (chose left) or 2 (chose right)

real<lower=0, upper=1> leftprob[nTrials]; 

real<lower=0, upper=1> leftvol[nTrials];  //rewards are normalized by max reward

real<lower=0, upper=1> rightprob[nTrials];

real<lower=0, upper=1> rightvol[nTrials];  //rewards are normalized by max reward

 

}

 

parameters {

real rho; //exponential of utility function

real alpha;  //parameter for probability weighting function

real lambda; //softmax parameter

}

 

 

model {

 

real p_choose_r;

real Rval[nTrials];

real Lval[nTrials];

 

//Priors

lambda ~ normal(1, 1); 

rho ~ normal(1, 1);

alpha ~ normal(1, 1);

 

for (trial_i in 1:nTrials) {

 

    Rval[trial_i] <- exp(-(-log(rightprob[trial_i]))^alpha)*(rightvol[trial_i]^rho);

    Lval[trial_i] <- exp(-(-log(leftprob[trial_i]))^alpha)*(leftvol[trial_i]^rho);

 

    p_choose_r <- 1/(1+exp(-lambda*(Rval[trial_i]-Lval[trial_i])));

    

    if (choices[trial_i] == 2){      

            increment_log_prob(log(p_choose_r)); //log-likelihood

            }

    else{

           increment_log_prob(log(1-p_choose_r)); //log-likelihood

    }

  }

}

 



Any suggestions are greatly appreciated!!

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rejecting initial value: Gradient evaluated at the initial value is not finite.
parts:
You want to track down whee things go off the rails in
terms of derivatives. I don't know if diagnostic mode is
available in MatlabStan, but you could use that to see which
derivatives aren't finite.

You don't want to do this by hand:
> p_choose_r <- 1/(1+exp(-lambda*(Rval[trial_i]-Lval[trial_i])));

we have inv_logit() defined. And even better, log_inv_logit()
and log1m_inv_logit(), which are what you really need for more
stability.

- Bob

parts: Oh, and what you really want is to replace all of this:

> if (choices[trial_i] == 2){
>
> increment_log_prob(log(p_choose_r)); //log-likelihood
>
> }
>
> else{
>
> increment_log_prob(log(1-p_choose_r)); //log-likelihood

with

(choices[trial_i] == 2) ~ bernoulli_logit(logit_p_choose_r);

so you don't need the conditional, the increment_log_prob,
and you don't need to do the logit fiddling yourself. then
you define the variable

logit_p_choose_r <- lambda * (Rval[trial_i] - Lval[trial_i]);

Really, you can just keep vectorizing at that point, but I'd
get it working before worrying about efficiency.

- Bob

Many thanks!!
Christine

parts:
I'm going through old list emails and saw this never got answered.
Did you get your install issues sorted out? You really want to make
sure to use dependencies=TRUE when installing rstan itself.

You usually don't want to do something like turn zeroes into arbitrary
small numbers---it's an indication something's wrong in the formulation of
the model. For instance, using a lognormal() for something that can take
on the value 0.

- Bob
